title: PRIOR: Pre-Call Reasoning in SFT and Its Influence on Tool-Use Retention under RL
abstract: arXiv:2611.33648v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Tool use learned during supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is not always retained during reinforcement learning (RL). We study how properties of SFT data may affect this retention by constructing Low, Medium, and High SFT datasets with approximately matched token budgets but different tool-call depths. Under the same RL recipe, the three initializations reach similar RL training accuracy yet exhibit markedly different tool-use dynamics: tool initiation increases in Low, declines in Medium, and collapses in High. We observe that these datasets also differ substantially in the amount of reasoning preceding each tool call. In particular, High trajectories contain considerably less pre-call reasoning, motivating the hypothesis that pre-call reasoning may affect how well tool use is calibrated and, consequently, whether the corresponding behaviors are retained during RL. An idealized theoretical analysis provides a selective-retention view of this

translated_title: PRIOR：SFT中的调用前推理及其对强化学习下工具使用保持能力的影响
translated_abstract: 在监督微调（SFT）阶段学习到的工具使用能力并不总能在强化学习（RL）阶段得以保持。我们通过构建Low、Medium和High三个SFT数据集来研究SFT数据的特性如何影响这种保持能力，这三个数据集具有大致匹配的token预算，但工具调用深度不同。在相同的RL训练方案下，三种初始模型达到了相近的RL训练准确率，却表现出显著不同的工具使用动态：Low组的工具调用发起率上升，Medium组下降，而High组则出现崩溃。我们观察到这些数据集在每次工具调用之前的推理量上也存在显著差异。特别是，High数据集的轨迹包含明显更少的调用前推理，由此引出一个假设：调用前推理可能影响工具使用的校准程度，进而决定相应行为在RL过程中是否被保持。理想化的理论分析为这一现象提供了“选择性保持”的视角。
tldr: 该研究通过控制token预算下的工具调用深度实验，揭示SFT数据中工具调用前的推理量是决定强化学习后工具使用行为能否保持的关键因素——调用前推理越少，RL训练中工具使用越容易崩溃。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that the amount of pre-call reasoning in SFT data is a key factor determining whether tool-use behavior is retained after RL—trajectories with less pre-call reasoning tend to suffer tool-use collapse during RL training.
